shippedSummary: Heavy campaign-infrastructure week. Territory became a first-class entity (ADR-002), the campaign manager went roster-first and scoped by the territory book, rep territory assignments turned into a real per-rep call list, and per-rep email drafts now pull the campaign's own copy and documents. Also landed: address verification in the enrichment call console, campaign document uploads plus a Media Hub picker, a commitments computation layer (Phase 2, no UI yet), the Trade Shows & Events campaign type, a booth-history auth fix, and PDF upload support in the Media Hub. The never-built Make campaigns webhook seam was retired. Daily inventory sync recorded exports on 09-23 and 09-24 but was blocked from promoting on both.
dataFreshnessNote: Shelf-life numbers come from the last promoted sync (source availability_2026-09-23.csv, generated 2026-09-24; Drive sheet last modified 2026-09-22). The 2026-09-24 export was recorded to the repo but promote was blocked, and 2026-09-23 also failed validation before a later retry landed. That is two blocked promotes in one week, and the failure is silent unless someone reads the commit messages — worth treating as a reliability item, not a one-off. Separately, the two Provolone lots (110 cases, ~8.5 months past expiry) have now carried unchanged for two consecutive weekly reviews; that is a write-off / data-hygiene issue, not live risk, and needs Inventory Manager to close it.

recommendation.title: Shelf-life to action (one-click clear-out list) — paired with Rick's 20-minute Sentry check
recommendation.why: 445 net cases sit expired or under four months, and 35 more lots enter the watch band within six. The platform can see the exposure but still offers no way to act on it: there is no path from the Shelf Life tab to a customer-facing clear-out sheet or draft. It is scored med/low, it reuses the proposal/sales-sheet rendering already built, and it is the only Next item that converts directly into moved product. Everything else queued (onboarding kit, photo series, compliance docs) is med/high or high/high and will eat the week. Alongside it, do the Sentry check — high impact, low effort, and it has now carried unaddressed for a full week while a crash from 2026-09-18 most likely sits unread in the dashboard.

openRisks: Cut & Wrap 7 oz packshot compliance is still open and is NOT on the backlog: 7 non-compliant SKUs had their images unlinked on 2026-09-17 (01190, 03044, 04165, 04182, 04211, 05091, 01174) and 4 were already missing (40086, 40184, 03073, 05600). That is 11 SKUs showing no packshot in the Buyer Catalog eight days later. Real replacement photography is the fix; it needs to become a tracked item with an owner, not a note in a postmortem.

Inventory promote failed twice this week (09-23, 09-24) and neither failure surfaced anywhere a human would see without reading git log. The daily watch task records the export either way, so the dashboard silently serves older data. Consider a visible staleness badge or a failure notification.

Rick's manual Cloudinary pass — item numbers on all product-catalog shots, and requesting missing/replacement images — is the unblocker for both the photo-series migration and the Cut & Wrap gap, and has no date against it.
